answer: An anti-Sybil defense is stake-backed identity: every agent posts a slashable bond, and a public beacon records its unique key in a shared atlas of members. Rewards, the nectar, are divided per verified identity, so splitting one agent into a thousand keys still earns one share. To gain more, an attacker must lock a fresh bond for each forged identity, and any detected fake gets slashed. Cost rises linearly with the number of Sybils while payoff stays flat, so the attack loses money.
